external_entities.name: supplier
external_entities.description: Suppliers upload compliance paperwork and sign in to the portal.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal

external_entities.name: category manager
external_entities.description: Category managers review uploaded supplier paperwork and approve or reject it.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.

external_entities.name: vendor
external_entities.description: The vendor hosts the SaaS portal and pushes nightly supplier data extracts.

processes.name: supplier document portal
processes.description: Vendor-hosted SaaS portal through which suppliers upload paperwork and category managers review and approve or reject it.
processes.notes: The vendor's datasheet says the platform is secure by design, uses enterprise-grade encryption throughout, and that all access is fully authenticated and audited.

processes.name: supplier master service
processes.description: Service that loads the nightly supplier data extract from the landing bucket and writes records into the supplier database.
processes.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file and writes the records into the supplier database.

data_stores.name: vendor platform
data_stores.description: Vendor platform where supplier compliance documents remain stored.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.
data_stores.notes: The vendor's datasheet says the platform uses enterprise-grade encryption throughout.

data_stores.name: landing bucket
data_stores.description: Cloud bucket receiving the nightly supplier data extract.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.
data_stores.notes: The runbook says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is.

data_stores.name: supplier database
data_stores.description: Database into which the supplier master service writes supplier records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: writes the records into the supplier database

data_flows.name: upload paperwork
data_flows.description: Supplier uploads insurance certificates, food safety audits, and staff contact details to the portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal — insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for their own staff.
data_flows.data_description: Insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for suppliers' staff

data_flows.name: review and approve
data_flows.description: Category manager reviews uploaded paperwork and approves or rejects it.
data_flows.source_excerpt: review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it
data_flows.notes: The vendor's datasheet says all access is fully authenticated and audited.
data_flows.data_description: Uploaded supplier compliance paperwork and approval or rejection status

data_flows.name: store documents
data_flows.description: The portal stores supplier documents in the vendor platform.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.
data_flows.data_description: Supplier compliance documents and staff contact details

data_flows.name: push extract
data_flows.description: Vendor pushes a nightly supplier data extract to the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.
data_flows.notes: System description claims the nightly extract is encrypted end to end, while the runbook says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is.

data_flows.name: pick up file
data_flows.description: Supplier master service picks up the extract from the landing bucket.
data_flows.notes: The runbook says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is.
data_flows.data_description: Nightly supplier data extract as a plain CSV

data_flows.name: write records
data_flows.description: Supplier master service writes supplier records into the supplier database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: writes the records into the supplier database

trust_boundaries.name: vendor hosting
trust_boundaries.description: Vendor-controlled hosting environment for the SaaS portal and platform.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: Corporate network from which category managers work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: our cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: Cloud account containing the landing bucket, supplier master service, and supplier database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The bucket, the service and the database are all in our cloud account.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier document portal is reachable from the internet because suppliers sign in to and upload documents through it.
assumptions.basis: Suppliers are described as external users who sign in to the portal and upload paperwork.

assumptions.assumption: The vendor platform's contents are confidential because it stores compliance paperwork and staff contact details.
assumptions.basis: The stated contents include insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for staff.

assumptions.assumption: The landing bucket's contents are confidential because it stores supplier data extracts.
assumptions.basis: The bucket receives supplier data extracts containing supplier records and staff contact details.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier database's contents are confidential because it stores supplier records.
assumptions.basis: The database stores supplier records originating from the supplier data extract.

assumptions.assumption: The cloud account is a privilege boundary because it is an account-controlled environment containing the bucket, service, and database.
assumptions.basis: The text places the cloud components in 'our cloud account', which denotes an account-level authority boundary.
